title: Random numbers and their tests
subtitle: Computers cannot be random, so we build generators whose output passes every test for randomness we can think of.

props.title: What we need from a generator
props.body: We want numbers that look uniformly distributed on [0, 1) and independent. Practical needs: fast, reproducible (same seed, same stream — essential for debugging), a long period before repeating, and the ability to produce several independent streams. Since an algorithm produces them they are pseudo-random.

lcg.title: The linear congruential method
lcg.body: Xn+1 = (a·Xn + c) mod m; Un = Xn/m. With a = 5, c = 3, m = 16, X₀ = 7 the sequence is 7 6 1 8 11 10 5 12 15 14 9 0 3 2 13 4 7 — it visits all 16 values before repeating (full period yes). The Hull–Dobell theorem: full period m iff c and m are coprime, a−1 is divisible by every prime factor of m, and by 4 if m is divisible by 4. A poor choice (a = 4, c = 0, m = 16, X₀ = 1) cycles early: period 1. A multiplicative (c = 0) generator can reach at most m−1.

chi.title: Testing uniformity: χ² and Kolmogorov–Smirnov
chi.body: The chi-square test splits [0,1) into k classes and compares observed counts Oᵢ with the expected n/k: χ² = Σ(Oᵢ − Eᵢ)²/Eᵢ; reject uniformity if it exceeds the critical value for k−1 degrees of freedom (14.07 for 8 classes at 5%). The Kolmogorov–Smirnov test compares the empirical CDF with the ideal diagonal: D = max gap, critical value ≈ 1.36/√n. Here χ² = 0 and D = 0.0625.

other.title: Other tests: gap, poker, autocorrelation
other.body: Uniformity is not enough — the sequence 0.1, 0.2, 0.3… is uniform but not random. Tests of independence: the gap test (gaps between occurrences of a digit should be geometric), the poker test (frequencies of patterns such as all different, one pair, three of a kind), runs tests (lengths of ascending/descending runs), and autocorrelation (correlation between Ui and Ui+k should be near 0).
other.steps: Poker test on 3-digit groups: probability all three digits differ = 10·9·8/10³. Exactly one pair: 3·10·9/10³ = 0.27; all same 10/10³ = 0.01. Total 1.00.

dist.title: Generating other distributions
dist.body: Given U ~ Uniform(0,1): the inverse transform method sets X = F⁻¹(U). For the exponential with rate λ, F(x) = 1 − e^(−λx), so X = −ln(1−U)/λ. Others: rejection sampling, composition (mix distributions), convolution (sum of variables: Erlang = sum of exponentials). Discrete: divide [0,1) into intervals of the given probabilities.
dist.steps: Generate an exponential(λ = 2) variate from U = 0.6. ln 0.4 = −0.916.

summary.title: Summary
summary.body:
• LCG: X ← (aX + c) mod m; full period needs Hull–Dobell.
  • Test uniformity (χ², KS) and independence (runs, gaps, autocorrelation).
  • Inverse transform: X = F⁻¹(U).
